tool.name: domain_reputation
tool.description:
Look up a domain or IP across 5 free public reputation sources. High-signal context: a "clean" target with an IP on URLhaus is a real finding (someone else compromised the shared host); a flagged domain you own is an incident-response lead.
| Source | Covers | Auth | |---|---|---| | **URLhaus** (abuse.ch) | domain + IP | none | | **Spamhaus DBL** | domain | none (low-volume) | | **Spamhaus ZEN** | IP | none (low-volume) | | **Google Safe Browsing** | domain + URL | `STRIX_GSB_KEY` | | **AbuseIPDB** | IP | `STRIX_ABUSEIPDB_KEY` |
The tool auto-detects whether `target` is a domain or an IP. For domains, it also resolves up to 3 A records and runs the IP-only sources (ZEN, AbuseIPDB) against each — catches "clean domain pointed at compromised shared host" cases. URL-shaped input is auto-stripped to its hostname. Private / loopback / link-local IPs are rejected.
Severity tuning: - **High** (CWE-453, malicious_target) — URLhaus active listing OR AbuseIPDB confidence ≥ 75%. - **Medium** — Spamhaus DBL listed; Google Safe Browsing flagged; AbuseIPDB confidence 25–74%. - **Low** — URLhaus historical entry; Spamhaus ZEN listed; AbuseIPDB confidence 1–24%.
Per-source dedup: at most one finding per (severity × source-id) so multiple URLhaus URLs collapse to ONE URLhaus finding. Per-source verdicts still live in `result["sources"]` for the agent.
Each finding carries `description_plain` + `recommended_action` tailored to the source: URLhaus / GSB hits → assume compromised, trigger IR workflow; Spamhaus DBL hits → fix root cause (SPF/DMARC misconfig + compromised mailbox) then request delisting; AbuseIPDB high-confidence hits → audit for compromised hosts, rotate keys, request delisting.
`verification_status=needs_review` since reputation lists can carry stale entries; the agent should follow up by inspecting the URLhaus / GSB references in the finding before treating any single hit as a confirmed compromise.
Cache: per-target JSON cache under `~/.strix/domain_rep_cache/`, 6-hour TTL. Stale-cache served on full-source failure (fail-open with `error` populated). Disable with `STRIX_DOMAIN_REP_NO_CACHE=1`.
Composes with cluster-A safety: rate-limit applies to outbound HTTP requests; DNS-RBL queries are throttled by the DNS resolver's own timeout. `--exclude-path` doesn't apply since the URLs are URLhaus / Google / AbuseIPDB / Spamhaus, not the customer's domain.

parameter.name: target
parameter.description: Domain (e.g. `example.com`, `app.example.com`) or IPv4 address (e.g. `198.51.100.42`). URL-shaped input (`https://example.com/`) is auto-stripped to the hostname. Private / loopback / link-local IPs are rejected.

returns.description:
{success, target, target_type, queried_at, from_cache, sources: {urlhaus: {listed, status, urls_count, ...}, spamhaus_dbl: {listed, codes, kinds} | {skipped}, spamhaus_zen: [{ip, listed, codes, kinds}, ...], google_safe_browsing: {listed, threats} | {skipped, reason}, abuseipdb: [{ip, listed, abuse_confidence, total_reports, ...}, ...], resolved_ips: [...]}, source_errors, findings_emitted}.
The agent should: 1. Surface high-severity findings prominently — they're actionable IR signals. 2. Note `source_errors.google_safe_browsing.skipped` / `abuseipdb[*].skipped` when keys aren't configured — coverage is partial in that case. 3. For shared-hosting cases (clean domain + flagged IP), distinguish "your code is fine, your host is compromised" in the report.
